title_zh: 中英双语同一套代码：Transloco + 路由分层，踩坑实录
title_en: Chinese + English in One Codebase: Transloco + Layered Routing, Every Mistake Documented
desc_zh: 用一套代码同时维护中文和英文，听起来只是加个翻译文件而已。实际上，路由分层、SEO hreflang、SSR 语言检测、翻译键管理……每一块都有坑。这篇文章是我把双语系统从零做到能跑、跑到不烦人的全过程记录。
desc_en: Maintaining Chinese and English in one codebase sounds like just adding a translation file. In practice, layered routing, SEO hreflang, SSR language detection, and translation key management all have traps. This is my complete record of building a bilingual system from scratch to production.
content_en:
## Why Bother With Bilingual My target audience has two segments: **Chinese-speaking users** (mainland China + overseas Chinese) and **English-speaking users** (global). Skipping one language means abandoning half the addressable market. The catch: bilingual isn't just "add a translation file." Routing, SEO, language switching, translation key management — each one needs deliberate design. --- ## Routing Architecture: Language Prefixes Two common approaches for bilingual URLs: - `puzzlepk.com/sudoku` + detect language from `Accept-Language` header (bad for SEO) - `puzzlepk.com/zh/sudoku` and `puzzlepk.com/en/sudoku` (each language has its own URL) I chose the second. Angular's route structure: ```typescript export const routes: Routes = [ { path: ':lang', // captures zh / en component: LangWrapperComponent, children: [ { path: '', component: HomeComponent }, { path: 'games/sudoku', loadComponent: () => import('./games/sudoku/...') }, // ... all games and pages ] }, { path: '', redirectTo: '/zh', pathMatch: 'full' }, ]; ``` `LangWrapperComponent` reads the `:lang` param and tells Transloco to switch: ```typescript export class LangWrapperComponent implements OnInit { ngOnInit() { const lang = this.route.snapshot.params['lang']; if (lang === 'zh' || lang === 'en') { this.transloco.setActiveLang(lang); } } } ``` --- ## Transloco: Runtime i18n Angular's official i18n is compile-time — it produces separate bundles for each language. I wanted **one build, language switched at runtime.** Transloco solves this. ```typescript // inline JSON at build time — no HTTP requests for translations import zh from '../../assets/i18n/zh.json'; import en from '../../assets/i18n/en.json'; export class TranslocoHttpLoader implements TranslocoLoader { getTranslation(lang: string): Observable { return of({ zh, en }[lang] ?? {}); } } ``` In templates: `{{ t('home.title') }}` In TypeScript: `this.i18n.t('game.sudoku.name')()` — returns a Signal, reactive by default. --- ## Translation Key Management The most common bilingual failure: keys added in Chinese but forgotten in English, or keys named differently across files. My rule: **`zh.json` is the single source of truth.** New keys go in `zh.json` first, then `en.json`. A quick script finds drift: ```javascript const zh = require('./src/assets/i18n/zh.json'); const en = require('./src/assets/i18n/en.json'); const missing = Object.keys(zh).filter(k => !en[k]); console.log(missing.length ? 'Missing in en.json:' : 'All keys present!', missing); ``` --- ## SEO: hreflang Tags Tell search engines about the relationship between language variants: ```html ``` `x-default` specifies the fallback when the user's language isn't listed. I defaulted to Chinese because early traffic skewed Chinese. --- ## The SSR Pitfall That Took Two Days During SSR rendering, `ActivatedRoute` params are async. My `LangWrapperComponent` couldn't set the active language in time, so Transloco fell back to rendering key names instead of values: ```html

Puzzle PK

home.title

``` Fix: parse the language from the request URL in an `APP_INITIALIZER` on the server side, so Transloco knows the active language before any component renders. --- ## Bilingual Content Workflow UI strings are the easy part. Blog posts, game descriptions, achievement text — all need both languages. My workflow: 1. Write in Chinese first (faster, more natural in native language) 2. Use Claude for an English draft 3. Manually edit technical vocabulary and tone 4. Store both in the database (`title_zh` / `title_en`) 5. Frontend reads the active-language field Writing bilingual content takes ~1.5× the time of Chinese-only, not 2× — translation from a draft is much faster than writing from scratch. --- *Next: **[07] Sudoku Deep Dive** — puzzle generation algorithms, difficulty grading, and PK mode state sync.*
